title: You Think Hardship Teaches Brains to Quit, Yet Freezing Is Default Until Control Wakes
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Martin Seligman & Steven Maier (1967-2016): Learned Helplessness & the Prefrontal-Raphe Passivity Twist, grounded in Martin E. Seligman, Steven F. Maier (1967) (Journal of Experimental Psychology). Empirical findings show that in 1967 at the University of Pennsylvania, graduate students Martin Seligman, Steven Maier, and Bruce Overmier designed a 'triadic yoked' experiment separating physical stress from behavioral control.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how brainstem, ventromedial prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that group 1 ('Escapable') could terminate mild brief discomfort immediately by pressing a head panel with its nose; Group 2 ('Yoked Inescapable') received the EXACT same microsecond-by-microsecond duration and intensity wired in series from Group 1, except its panel was disconnected; Group 3 received none.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Martin E. Seligman, Steven F. Maier (1967). Failure to escape traumatic shock. Journal of Experimental Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0024514
- Steven F. Maier, Martin E. P. Seligman (2016). Learned helplessness at fifty: Insights from neuroscience. Psychological Review. https://doi.org/10.1037/rev0000033
- Steven F. Maier, Martin E. Seligman (1976). Learned helplessness: Theory and evidence. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General. https://doi.org/10.1037/0096-3445.105.1.3

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
